attachments.origin_landmark: oblique line of the thyroid cartilage and the side of the cricoid (the laryngeal cartilages are not modeled as skeletal elements in this pass -- approximated via the adjacent hyoid attachment region)

actions: its cricopharyngeus part acts as the upper oesophageal sphincter

functional_compartments.name: Thyropharyngeus (oblique part)
functional_compartments.function_note: Oblique fibres from the thyroid cartilage. Killian's dehiscence -- the weak triangle between these oblique fibres and the transverse cricopharyngeus below -- is where a Zenker's pharyngeal pouch herniates.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

functional_compartments.name: Cricopharyngeus (transverse part)
functional_compartments.function_note: Transverse fibres from the cricoid, tonically contracted as the upper oesophageal sphincter and relaxing to admit the bolus. Failure of that relaxation is the mechanism behind Zenker's diverticulum, and the target of cricopharyngeal myotomy.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
